title: Tenant-aware write-path QoS, index mapping, and retention playbook for audit ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Playbook to make the audit logging write path tenant-aware with QoS/ingest shaping, deterministic index mapping, and retention lifecycle that enforces cost controls while preserving forensic fidelity for RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML admin events.
background: We ingest high-volume audit events (SSO assertions, RBAC grant/revoke, admin UI actions). Current pipeline has coarse tenant throttles and monolithic indices, leading to hot shards, unpredictable costs, and slow retention compaction. The RBAC v2 rollout increases privileged events and demand for fine-grained search. Need a repeatable operational plan to stabilize costs and SLOs while retaining necessary audit fidelity for compliance.
goals: 1) Per-tenant QoS that prevents noisy tenants from impacting global SLOs. 2) Deterministic index mapping and partitioning that keeps searches for privileged events fast. 3) Retention policy that balances forensic retention vs storage cost with easy admin overrides. 4) Captured metadata for SSO/SAML and RBAC v2 to enable audit trails and complaint investigations.
design_decisions: Adopt a two-tier write-path: hot fast-path (recent events, sub-minute query SLO) and cold append-only store (nearline for long-term retention).
Per-tenant token-bucket shaper at ingress that is enforced by the write proxy; soft limit triggers sampling and hard limit drops oldest non-privileged events.

Index mapping will include: tenant_id (keyword), event_type (keyword), privilege_level (enum), saml_assertion_hash (keyword), sso_provider (keyword), requester_principal_id (keyword), rbac_change_id (keyword), event_ts (date).
Partition by time + tenant_bucket: daily indices for high-volume tenants, weekly for low-volume tenants. Tenant buckets defined by 95th-percentile ingestion rate to minimize number of hot indices.

Retention tiers: 30 days hot, 365 days warm (compressed), immutable archive beyond 365 days in coldstore (object storage) with on-demand restores. Privileged events (privilege_level >= high) keep 3 years in warm tier before coldstore.
Admin overrides: RBAC-based admin controls (RBAC v2) to mark a tenant or a specific audit query with elevated retention; actions recorded as audit events themselves.
Cost controls: per-tenant budget meter that emits billing alerts and automatically applies stricter sampling when budget thresholds hit.
Sampling: deterministic reservoir sampling keyed on tenant_id+event_type to preserve representative distribution when sampling is applied.
Backpressure: upstream clients receive HTTP 429 with retry-after when per-tenant soft limit exceeded; router supports graceful fallback to a lower-fidelity telemetry event when configured.
Security: SAML assertions are hashed and stored as saml_assertion_hash; full assertion stored only in encrypted coldstore blobs with KMS keys and strict audit access.
Observability: telemetry per-tenant ingestion rate, dropped_events, sampling_rate, hot_shard_count, per-tenant storage bytes, and retention exceptions.
Compatibility: ensure compatibility with existing query layer by providing an index aliasing layer that hides partitioning from consumers.
Migration: rolling reindex for top 50 tenants into new mapping; lower-volume tenants migrate on first write to new bucket.
Failure semantics: write-to-warmpath is idempotent via event sequence id; coldstore uploads are retried with exponential backoff and dead-letter queue for manual reconciliation.
data_schema_changes: Add fields: privilege_level (low|medium|high), tenant_bucket (int), saml_assertion_hash, rbac_change_id, original_payload_ref (coldstore URI). Deprecate storing raw SAML in hot index; raw stored encrypted in coldstore only.
partitioning_strategy: Tiered time+tenant bucketing: compute tenant_bucket by 95th percentile ingestion per tenant over trailing 7 days. High-volume tenants get dedicated daily indices; medium-volume tenants share per-tenant-bucket indices; low-volume tenants are grouped into weekly rollup indices. Shard count per index sized by target shard size (20-40GB) to avoid hotspots.
retention_strategy: Retention tiers: hot (30 days, searchable), warm (31-365 days, compressed, searchable with reduced IO), cold (>=366 days, object store, query via restore). Privileged events override retention to 3y warm. Admin can request ad-hoc extension via RBAC v2 controlled UI; each override creates an audit event and a retention ticket in the retention engine.
cost_controls: 1) Per-tenant monthly soft and hard ingestion budgets. 2) Auto-sampling triggers: at 70% soft budget apply deterministic sampling; at 90% apply aggressive sampling for non-privileged events; at hard budget (100%) drop non-essential writes and surface alerts to tenant admin. 3) Storage compaction jobs compress warm indices weekly and record estimated savings. 4) Coldstore lifecycle move scheduled during off-peak windows to reduce retrieval costs.
admin_controls_and_audit: Admin UI exposes: tenant budget, current ingestion rate, sampling profile, retention overrides, and the ability to request temporary burst credits. All admin actions go through RBAC v2: require 'audit.admin' role and SSO MFA for retention overrides longer than 30 days. Every admin action emits an audit event with requestor_principal_id, action, reason, and ticket ref.
sso_saml_fields_to_capture: Capture saml_assertion_hash, sso_provider, assertion_verified (boolean), nameid_pseudonym (hashed), assertion_timestamp, unique_assertion_id. Store raw assertion encrypted in coldstore with a KMS-wrapped key per-tenant. Do not store cleartext PII in hot indices.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Deploy write-proxy shaper and per-tenant metering in staging, smoke test with synthetic tenants. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Migrate top 10 high-volume tenants to dedicated indices and verify query SLOs. Phase 3 (4 weeks): Enable sampling and budget enforcement for experimental tenant cohort. Phase 4 (2 weeks): Gradual rollout org-wide with monitoring and a 2-week rollback window. Maintain a migration runbook for index reindexing with abort hooks.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboards and alerts: per-tenant ingestion QPS, dropped_events count > 0 over 5min, shard_hotspot_ratio > 0.1, sampling_rate increase > 10% in 5min, storage_bytes_growth_rate > baseline. Pager duty for storage budget breaches for enterprise customers. SLA: 99.9% write success for hot path under normal load.
testing_plan: Unit tests for shaper logic and reservoir sampler. Integration tests: simulate noisy tenant and validate 429/billing behavior, validate privileged event preservation, verify index aliases and query responses. Load test: synthetic 10x peak to validate shard sizing and backpressure. Data verification: sample replays to ensure deterministic sampling preserves distributions.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive sampling might remove critical forensic signals. Mitigation: sampling rules whitelist event_types tagged as high_privilege; retention override audit trail. Risk: Hot shards for mid-size tenants. Mitigation: dynamic tenant_bucket recalculation and autosplit policy. Risk: Admin overrides abused. Mitigation: require 'audit.admin' role and MFA for long-lived overrides and log all overrides with ticket references.
open_questions: What is the cost threshold (USD/month) to auto-apply burst credits vs. apply sampling?
Should privileged events include additional fields (caller_ip) in hot index or only in coldstore?
How often should tenant_bucket be recomputed (daily vs hourly) to react to bursty tenants without causing index churn?
Do we need per-customer KMS keys or shared KMS with tenant-wrapped keys for coldstore encryption?
